commands.review_summary:
Adds bounded reuse of a recent successful hosted CI run when a rebased PR head has a patch-identical diff, plus tests for acceptance, rejection, and provenance paths.

PR surface: Tests +328, Other +229. Total +557 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: not applicable. this is a new maintainer-tooling behavior rather than a report of broken user behavior. The cited unit tests exercise simulated paths, but no real `prepare-run` evidence is attached.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A maintainer must confirm the hosted-CI equivalence policy; the contributor should then correct the declaration and attach real behavior proof.

target.title: chore(pr): reuse green hosted CI from patch-identical pre-rebase heads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The hosted-CI gate in `scripts/pr prepare-run` requires a successful `CI` run on the exact head SHA. During a fast-moving `main`, every content-identical rebase discards green CI and forces a full re-run: on 2026-07-18 this cost roughly four full CI cycles across four widget PRs, each rebase triggered by unrelated `main` churn. The Testbox side of prepare already honors "patch-identical pre-rebase run green within 24 hours"; the hosted-CI check did not.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/verify-pr-hosted-gates.mjs` now mirrors the Testbox reuse semantics. When no qualifying run exists for the current head, it examines up to five recent successful branch CI runs (`pull_request` runs named `CI`, or the exact release-gate dispatch shape), requires them to be ≤24h old, fetches missing commits with a guarded single `git fetch`, and accepts only when `git diff <merge-base> <head> | git patch-id --stable` matches between the current head and the candidate (each against its own merge base with `origin/main`). Acceptance is logged with the reused head, run id, and age, and recorded in `.local/gates-hosted-checks.json` (`reusedFromSha`, `reusedRunId`, `patchIdMatched: true`, mode `patch-identical-pre-rebase`) so merge provenance stays auditable. Exact-head success still short-circuits; every ambiguity (fetch failure, merge-base error, stale, patch mismatch) skips the candidate and the gate fails exactly as before. Changelog-only mode, release-gate matching, and Testbox logic untouched.

Accepted contract note: `git patch-id --stable` is whitespace-insensitive by design — the same equivalence git itself uses for cherry-pick detection; flagged in review and consciously accepted.

## User Impact

Maintainer tooling only: a rebase that changes no content no longer costs a CI cycle at prepare time; anything content-changing still requires fresh exact-head CI.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/verify-pr-hosted-gates.test.ts` — 55 tests passing (patch-identical accept, patch-different reject, stale reject, unfetchable skip, exec-error fail-closed, exact-head short-circuit, provenance fields, existing gate behaviors).
- `node --check` and `git diff --check` clean.
- Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`): two findings accepted and fixed (scheduled-workflow fallback preserved; 64 MiB git subprocess buffer); whitespace-insensitivity objection consciously rejected as the explicit contract.

Release-note context: none needed (maintainer tooling).
